Here’s a simple way to segregate wet and dry waste — it’s easy once you get used to it 👇

♻️ 1. Wet Waste (Biodegradable)

These are organic wastes that can decompose naturally.
🟢 Examples:

Food leftovers

Fruit & vegetable peels

Tea leaves, coffee grounds

Egg shells

Flowers, leaves, garden waste


🪣 Where to keep: Green bin or bucket
💡 Tip: Line it with newspaper (not plastic) or compostable bag to keep it clean.


---

🧺 2. Dry Waste (Non-Biodegradable)

These are recyclable materials that do not rot.
🔵 Examples:

Paper, cardboard

Plastic bottles, wrappers, containers

Glass bottles, metal cans

Old clothes, packaging materials


🪣 Where to keep: Blue bin or another separate container
💡 Tip: Make sure items are clean and dry before putting them here (no food stains).


---

🚫 Special Waste (to handle separately)

Some waste doesn’t fit either category:
⚠️ Examples:

Sanitary pads, diapers (put in red bin)

E-waste (batteries, chargers, bulbs)

Hazardous items (paint, chemicals)



---
